children: Shares in Vivendi fell after the French investment company reported a decline in first-half revenue dragged by weaker performance in its video-game subsidiary Gameloft.
The stock was down 4.7% at 1.52 euros in European morning trading. Year to date, shares have fallen around 35%.
For the first half, revenue fell to 140 million euros ($162.8 million) from 145 million euros for the same period a year earlier, due to the seasonality of Gameloft's game launches, Vivendi said.
Gameloft's revenue declined to 132 million euros from 143 million euros. In the second quarter, Gameloft's revenue fell 12.9% on a constant-currency basis.

"In a video game market under significant pressure, Gameloft demonstrated its strict cost control management and its strategic objective of rebalancing towards the PC/console segment," Chairman Yannick Bollore and Chief Executive Officer Arnaud de Puyfontaine said.
Major game releases and updates are scheduled for the second half of the year, Vivendi added.

Meanwhile, first-half adjusted earnings before interest and income taxes fell to 4 million euros from 18 million euros. The decline reflects a 21 million-euro hit from a collective mutual termination plan at the group's headquarters, it said.
Net profit for the period dropped to 28 million euros from 30 million euros a year earlier.

title: Vivendi Shares Fall After Revenue Decline on Weak Gameloft Performance
